column8: Comment

column5: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
column8: Absolutive is unmarked (-Ø) in Matses. Both S and O bear no case marker. Ergative A is marked with -n.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
column8: Matses 1st person singular pronouns follow ergative alignment: A=umbi/embi, S/O=ubi/ebi. The 1+2 inclusive nuki is neutral (invariant). Archaic 2pl forms are also neutral. Overall, singular pronouns are ergative.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
column8: Matses 2nd person singular (and plural, which has merged with singular) follows ergative alignment: A=mimbi, S/O=mibi. Archaic 2pl forms (miki, mitso) are neutral. The productive 2nd person form is ergative.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
column8: Matses 3rd person anaphora is Ø (zero) in all positions — effectively neutral/ergative since there is no distinct accusative form. The archaic 3pl ato is reported by some speakers but its alignment is uncertain. The 4th person (coreferential) ambi/abi follows ergative alignment.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
column8: Full NPs in Matses follow strict ergative-absolutive case marking: A marked with -n (ERG), S and O unmarked (-Ø, ABS). See ex. (2a,b): [dada iksa]-n 'bad man-ERG'.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
column8: No aspect-based split is documented for Matses. Fleck explicitly states: 'there are no typical split alignment systems in Mayoruna languages, such as splits conditioned by tense/aspect/mood' (p. 35). Ergative alignment applies regardless of aspect.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
column8: No aspect-based split documented. Ergative alignment on full NPs applies in perfective contexts. See ex. (2a): kues-o-sh 'hit-REC.PAST-3' with ergative A.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
column8: No tense-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies in past tense. Ex. (2a) uses recent past inflection with ergative A.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
column8: No tense-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies in non-past. Ex. (14b): debi-n mibi bun-e-k 'Davy-ERG 2ABS like-NPAST-INDIC'.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
column8: No mood-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies in indicative mood.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
column8: No mood-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies in non-indicative moods.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
column8: No realis/irrealis split documented. Ergative alignment applies in realis contexts.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
column8: No realis/irrealis split documented. Ergative alignment applies in irrealis contexts.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
column8: No agentivity-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies with agentive A. Note: extended intransitive verbs (§4) are an exception where both arguments are ABS, but this is a verb-class-based phenomenon, not agentivity-based.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
column8: No agentivity-based split documented. Psych-verbs and experiencer verbs in Matses are treated as transitive with the Experiencer in ergative case (p. 48). Ergative applies with non-agentive A.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
column8: No topicality-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies regardless of topicality of A.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
column8: No topicality-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies regardless of topicality of A.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
column8: No animacy-based split documented. Ergative alignment applies with animate A.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
column8: No animacy-based split documented for basic transitive clauses. Note: ex. (14d) shows that the ergative marker CANNOT be used with inanimate A in extended intransitive (bun) clauses, but this is specific to that verb class, not a general split.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
column8: Ergative alignment is documented in main clauses. This is the primary context described.

column5: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
column7: Fleck, D. (2010). Ergativity in the Mayoruna branch of the Panoan family. In Queixalós & Gildea (eds.), Ergativity in Amazonia. John Benjamins. §6.1, p. 55-57; ex. (27b), p. 56
column8: Ergative alignment has been extended to reanalyzed negative constructions (§6.1). Ex. (27b): tumi-n pe-enkio ik-o-sh 'man's.name-ERG eat-NEG AUX-PAST-3'. Ergative applies in non-main/subordinate clauses.

column5: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
column8: Yes, two conditioning factors: (1) VERB CLASS: extended intransitive verbs (bun 'want/like', bëshun 'forget', kudas 'not share') take two ABS arguments instead of ERG+ABS. (2) NOMINAL CLASS: singular pronouns are ergative; 1+2 inclusive nuki is neutral (invariant); archaic 2pl forms are neutral. Full NPs are consistently ergative.

column5: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
column8: Yes. On full nouns, ergative case is marked identically to genitive and instrumental: -n (with allomorph -ën after consonants). See ex. (2a): tumi-n opa 'Tumi-GEN dog' vs. dada iksa-n 'bad man-ERG'. Note: on pronouns, ergative and genitive differ in form.

column5: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
column8: Yes for instrumental: on full nouns, ergative and instrumental are both marked with -n. See ex. (2a): kueste-n 'stick-INST'. Comitative is expressed by a distinct postposition: -bëd 'Comitative' (p. 37). So: ergative = instrumental (same marker -n), but ergative ≠ comitative.
